onboarding_change_log.summary: Onboarding flow was completely unchanged between February and March. No deploys, no copy changes, no A/B test running.
onboarding_change_log.note: A constant can't explain a change. Separately, traffic-source mix shifted toward a lower-intent channel in the same window -- that's the thing that actually moved, and it's worse than the original claim implied.

benchmark_comparison.summary: The Q1 benchmark report defines retention as 30-day active; our internal number is 90-day active. The two are not comparable as published.
benchmark_comparison.note: The internal number isn't being disputed -- the benchmark's categories don't match it, so the comparison itself is invalid.

price_sensitivity_pulls.summary: Three independent data pulls (monthly, quarterly, and a targeted survey) all show the same segment ordering. No contradicting pull found.

support_response_data.summary: One support ticket thread mentions slow response as a factor in a single cancellation. No systematic churn-vs-response-time data exists.
support_response_data.note: Not enough evidence to kill OR confirm. The claim might be true -- there's just nothing here that proves or disproves it at scale.
